entries.title: Signing Pennsylvania
paragraphs: A short film shows Lemonhaze signing a physical print of Pennsylvania. Shared in July 2025, it records the artwork at the print table.
The accompanying description identifies SCR 310gsm paper and a print measuring 76 × 102 cm.

video.title: Lemonhaze signing a physical print of Pennsylvania
video.caption: Lemonhaze signing Pennsylvania · SCR 310gsm · 76 × 102 cm. Footage shared July 13, 2025.

entries.title: Good Night, off the screen
paragraphs: A large Good Night print is documented at the worktable, giving a sense of its scale and material presence.
The August 2025 record identifies SCR 310gsm paper, measuring 61 × 108.5 cm. It is an example of a particular physical presentation of the work.

images.alt: Good Night at the print table
images.caption: Good Night · SCR 310gsm · 61 × 108.5 cm. Photograph shared by Lemonhaze.

entries.title: Chanchanok’s Temple: inside the process
paragraphs: Sketches, collage, testing and generative texture meet in Chanchanok’s Temple. This process film moves through components of the image, experiments with different outputs, blending and the final surface.
The actual work is less linear than the film: Lemonhaze moves back and forth between tools, adjusting the components until they belong together. AI, Krita and p5.js each play a part.

entries.title: Smoke Break: a photograph, reworked
paragraphs: Smoke Break began with a photograph taken on a phone. A chair, a balcony and the landscape beyond became the starting material for a new image.

The photograph was redrawn with AI, manually modified in Krita, then brought into the artist’s code-based framework with its own set of textures. The place remains recognisable through the transformed colour and surface.

images.caption: Smoke Break, after drawing, colour and texture work.

entries.title: Building an image in layers
paragraphs: Paper and canvas textures, grid-like weaves, backgrounds, black ink and brushes each have a place in the paint engine. In the January 2025 account, the ink is drawn over the background and beneath the textures.
Small fragments of an output can be extracted, distorted and reapplied. This clipping and sampling brings depth and irregularity, much as a sampled sound can change a piece of music.

The recurring black marks connect to ballpoint drawings, early spray painting, and personal interpretations of ink wash. The finished image holds the balance between a considered composition and a rough, imperfect surface.

images.caption: A finished composition illustrating the layered approach.
Another finished composition from the same process account.

entries.title: Three works, three techniques
paragraphs: Revaler Straße 99 was digitally hand-drawn in Krita. Avant le Crépuscule combines AI, Krita and p5.js. From Berlin to Saigon is a generative p5.js work.
Together these separate works show an evolving approach to composition and surface, from small drawn forms to mixed tools and heavily textured code-based work.

images.caption: Avant le Crépuscule · AI, Krita and p5.js.

entries.title: One starting image, three directions
paragraphs: Glass Breaker, Off-Kilter and Mending Out began with the same starting image. Colours were mixed separately in Krita, then matched through the WebGL work.
Their shared beginning makes the differences worth looking at: colour and treatment move each image toward a distinct feeling. Their individual diary entries remain part of the original works.

images.caption: Glass Breaker, Off-Kilter and Mending Out.

entries.title: Colour that returns across different tools
paragraphs: Orange and purple recur across works made in different ways. Flashback and Soleil & Mer use code-defined colours; Debt Sentence and Smoke Break bring photography and manual colour work into coded textures.
Looking back in January 2026, Lemonhaze noticed this continuity without having planned it. The colour relationship travels further than any single technique.

entries.title: Marilyn, through four techniques
paragraphs: The recurring Marilyn / Monero subject passes through collage and Photomosh, a digitally hand-drawn fragmented portrait, AI with Krita, and p5.js. Each version asks something different of the available tools.
The Bootleg Remix originated as a GIF made and minted on Ethereum in 2021. The later versions place the subject within different parts of Lemonhaze’s Bitcoin practice.

images.caption: Bootleg Remix · collage and Photomosh; based on a Marilyn Monroe portrait.
Mending Fragments · digitally hand-drawn in Krita.

entries.title: Three stages of an experiment
paragraphs: An August 2023 comparison brings together Untitled, Degeneration #0 and Degeneration #2. Granular surfaces and geometric arrangements show different stages of an experiment with generative composition.
The comparison preserves a glimpse of the development between works, alongside the finished inscriptions.

images.caption: One of the three process examples shared in August 2023.

entries.title: Three tiny canvases, a change of approach
paragraphs: The Void began as a marker-on-paper sketch. Casa Flamingo reworked a recent oil painting. Khaosan was improvised on a fresh 50 × 50 canvas. Their files measured 777, 648 and 558 bytes respectively.

Larger images had become too expensive to inscribe. Making these small works changed the question: how could the work be created for Bitcoin, with its constraints present from the beginning? A period of small hand-drawn series followed.

images.alt: Casa Flamingo: pixels, painting and house
images.caption: Casa Flamingo, one of the three Tad Small works.

entries.title: Sushi: a small memory of Tenerife
paragraphs: Sushi remembers one of Lemonhaze’s last meals in Tenerife after several weeks with the team from his first official crypto job.
The small digitally hand-drawn works of Le Bar à Tapas made it possible to keep inscribing during a period of high fees. Ordinary moments became compact mementos.

entries.title: From Polaroid to fragmented works
paragraphs: Polaroid #5 and #7 sparked the fragmented approach that followed in Mending Fragments, Discography and World Tour during June and July 2023.

The technique connects them, while the subjects distinguish them: portraits in Mending Fragments, album covers in Discography, and country flags in World Tour. The music and places are part of an unfinished personal record.

images.alt: Polaroid and the start of fragmentation
images.caption: Polaroid example shared alongside the account of the fragmented works.

entries.title: Jardin Secret: beginning with a sketch
paragraphs: In July 2023, Lemonhaze was painting shapes and ideas for Jardin Secret. The photograph of Bonzai preserves a physical sketch from that period.
The series also includes Haiku, accompanied by the artist’s words: “Behind closed eyelids, / Silent gardens gently grow, / Secrets never known.”

entries.title: Small images, spare statements
paragraphs: Framed returns to being in the wrong place at the wrong time. Dark Days asks about losing control. Fading follows decay and echoes of the past; Polaroid aims to capture a moment simply.
These short descriptions sit alongside digitally hand-drawn Krita images. Their small scale leaves room for a mood or thought without explaining it away.

entries.title: Volatility: emotion, code and writing
paragraphs: Volatility draws a parallel between market fluctuations and the movement of emotional life: euphoria, despair and the search for balance.
It was Lemonhaze’s first officially released and sold generative collection, and the first where he deliberately explored personal, candid notes in the HTML headers.

entries.title: Berlin as a study in balance
paragraphs: The Berlin works are memories of the city in 2018, but their small Krita canvases were also a place to study composition and balance.
Palettes and structural ideas were sampled from AI sketches and experiments, an approach Lemonhaze first explored with Manifesto. The drawing and the reference material developed together.

entries.title: A wide canvas for the city
paragraphs: Downtown combines retro-wave references and the energy of urban life in a wide 16:9 format. Minimal textures accompany remembered metropolitan scenes.
The notes preserve more ordinary moments too: craving a visit to Mexico City, working for several days, and finally remembering to inscribe Good Night.

entries.title: Bento Box: a simple visual pleasure
paragraphs: Bento Box was described as digital delicacies crafted with code: carefully curated compositions for simplicity and visual pleasure.
Bento Box Nº1 was also called Los Angeles, in honour of @PARIS_sats.

entries.title: La Tentation: indulgence and control
paragraphs: An extended grid and vivid palettes give La Tentation its structure. Colour mixing and texture carry a tension between indulgence and restraint.
The series continues Lemonhaze’s work with code, holding an ordered composition alongside a more restless surface.

images.caption: La Tentation: an overview of the series.

entries.title: Unregulated Minds: returning to a state of mind
paragraphs: Unregulated Minds was inscribed on January 2, 2024. Its cursed inscriptions carry an interest in freedom of thought and the liberty to think beyond what feels comfortable.
Distribution came around Halloween and Bitcoin Whitepaper day that year. Lemonhaze had waited to return to the optimistic, energetic mindset in which the collection had been made.

entries.title: The Artifacts: individual works and shared memories
paragraphs: The Artifacts is an early grouping of individual 1/1s. Some works share techniques or memories without forming separate official collections.

Adriatic View, Himarë, Gjipe and Αθήνα return to travels through the Balkans in summer 2022. Blood, Lemon & Tango, Le Dessinateur, Biarritz and Playa Zicatela form another connection through mixed techniques and personal memories.

entries.title: DeVille: two waves of experimentation
paragraphs: DeVille #1–11 mainly combine AI images with p5.js texture. In #12–16, more manual modification and generative backgrounds enter the image. The two waves, made about a year apart, record that change in technique.
Each work also reconnects with its Cypherville ancestor through recursion and the creature’s original written description.

entries.title: What might we look like in 2490?
paragraphs: Portrait 2490 brings together ninety futuristic portraits of robots and humans. Released in March 2023, these early AI experiments ask what people might look like far into the future.
The portraits preceded Gentlemen. The collection also helped form the early community around the work: one collector encouraged Lemonhaze to set up a Discord server.

entries.title: A little distance from the work
paragraphs: Little Get Away grew alongside plans for a real break with the artist’s partner. It also meant a break from an intense focus on texture, turning toward minimal code-based landscapes.
The first getaway did not completely take his mind off work. The desire to step back became part of the work itself.

entries.title: Manufactured: individually written, collectively connected
paragraphs: The 420 Manufactured inscriptions have individually written HTML notes, including small greetings to collectors and builders. Beneath a series concerned with mass production sits a collection of personal writing.

Its engine also contains an archive of earlier inscription IDs. Those IDs become generative seeds inside the series, carrying earlier works into new outputs. Manufactured and Games share a family of parents, preserving their complementary relationship.
The 420 works were inscribed together on consecutive sats, then padded and separated. The Hosoi sale helped make that carefully planned process possible.

entries.title: La Carte: a remembered time card
paragraphs: La Carte abstracts the time cards once used by workers. Its inscription note returns to a piece of advice from Lemonhaze’s father: work hard, then reap the fruits of that labour. The artist adds a question—does that promise really hold for workers?
The image also became the source of a Manufactured palette. A song by Pagliaro, remembered from childhood, brings another association with work into the story.

images.alt: La Carte: artwork and later palette
images.caption: A later image carrying the La Carte palette.

entries.title: Palettes that travel between collections
paragraphs: Coral, from Candidly Yours, became the source of a Manufactured palette. La Carte made a similar journey from an earlier artwork into the later collection.

My Love connects Gentleman Nº1, 99 Francs and Five Roses. Colours were sampled, adjusted and carried into other series, with Deep Pink added for Five Roses in January 2024. The repeated palette holds together places and moments that otherwise look far apart.

images.alt: La Carte: artwork and later palette
images.caption: La Carte.

images.alt: La Carte: artwork and later palette
images.caption: The palette carried into a later work.

entries.title: Casa Flamingo: a place becomes an image
paragraphs: A tiny house under construction in Puerto Escondido became both a painted study and a small digital abstraction. The building, the painting and the pixel artwork appear together in the artist’s June 2023 photographs.

Casa Flamingo belongs to Tad Small, made when inscription costs prompted a different way of working. Lemonhaze returned to an oil painting that was not yet dry and translated it onto a tiny pixel canvas. The resulting file was 648 bytes.
The later interior photograph, shared in April 2026, shows the place after the early construction period.

images.alt: Finished interior of Casa Flamingo, photographed from the kitchen toward the terrace
images.caption: Casa Flamingo interior, shared April 9, 2026.

images.alt: Casa Flamingo: pixels, painting and house
images.caption: The painted study.

images.alt: Casa Flamingo: pixels, painting and house
images.caption: Another view of the painted study.

images.alt: Casa Flamingo: pixels, painting and house
images.caption: Casa Flamingo, the digital abstraction.

entries.title: Hosoi: texture and a turning point
paragraphs: Hosoi was the first work Lemonhaze made with the combination of AI, Krita and p5.js. The approach grew from wanting to inscribe higher-resolution work in September 2023. Tiny Bitcoin symbols form part of its texture.
Its public primary sale for 0.5 BTC in March 2024 became a milestone, and helped support the inscription of Manufactured. The technique continued through later individual works and collections.

entries.title: Paris: a promise of time together
paragraphs: The work holds a promise of going to Paris together, alongside an apology for being present and absent at once. The artist describes staying up working while his partner went to bed, hoping that the work would eventually make room for time away together.
Paris was included in OCM’s Digital Rosetta Stone.

entries.title: Chamber of Reflection: keeping the rough edges
paragraphs: AI sketches were compressed, cut and reworked in Krita before being combined with coded texture. Enlarging those fragments introduced blur, pixel scraps and ambiguity.
That roughness became part of the desired surface: a meeting of old and new, nature and technology, rather than a fault to smooth away.
Chamber of Reflection was included as Lot 592 in Sotheby’s Contemporary Discoveries in New York in February 2025.

related.label: Sotheby’s Contemporary Discoveries in Career Highlights

entries.title: The Mask: identity and performance
paragraphs: The Mask reaches beyond a reference to the 1994 film. It considers identity and performance, and the moment its character learns that he does not need the mask to be himself.
Jim Carrey’s energy and his wider reflections on life are also part of the artist’s stated reference.

entries.title: Tuna: a scene and a song
paragraphs: Tuna’s note points to the arrival in California in the film Blow, accompanied by Link Wray’s Rumble. A remembered scene and its music become a personal reference inside an abstract work.

entries.title: Shelling Out: ideas that stayed
paragraphs: Shelling Out nods to Nick Szabo’s essay on the origins of money, and to the effect Bitcoin and its early thinkers had on Lemonhaze’s life.
Its brief, unsigned header belongs to an early stage of writing inside inscriptions, before those notes grew into a regular and more extensive part of the practice.

entries.title: Le Hazy Night: waking with an image in mind
paragraphs: On August 7, 2023, Lemonhaze woke after seeing Japanese art the night before. It brought Van Gogh’s Japonaiserie to mind, followed by an attempt at a simple generative response to The Starry Night.
The inscription closes with a greeting to a future reader: a moment of recognition across an unknown span of time.

entries.title: La Pomme Pourrite: the way it is spoken
paragraphs: The spelling of La Pomme Pourrite is deliberate. It reflects how Lemonhaze says the word in Québécois French, preserving a spoken voice inside the title.
The existing inscription note ties the image to gratitude toward his partner and the aspiration to become a gentleman.

entries.title: Marilyn / Monero: exposure and privacy
paragraphs: Marilyn plays with the distance between public exposure and deliberate privacy. The Marilyn / Monero wordplay brings a hyper-visible figure alongside a desire for protection and concealment.
The diary section carries the idea into the writing: that day, the artist chooses to say nothing about his personal life.

entries.title: Dogmatic Structure: a chain and a lasting story
paragraphs: Dogmatic Structure holds a written interview with Fabled inside its HTML, alongside dated journal entries. The questions open onto the artist’s process, intuition, and wish for the work to outlive him. Images and writing become ways to keep a record that can be revisited.

The interview describes the artwork as a lasting reminder to oneself, and the writing as messages left for future readers. The hope is that someone will eventually explore the inscriptions, connect their details, and piece together the wider story.

A later entry gives permanence a smaller, physical starting point. Having lost a chain in Sin City, the artist puts this one “on-chain” so it cannot leave him again. The personal incident and the larger wish to preserve a life meet in the same work.

excerpts.text: I can count on one hand the people who truly understand what I’m doing here, inscribing my art and my thoughts on Bitcoin. My goal is longevity, not of my body but rather of my story. My journey, the journey of a simple man or not so simple after all. Just a human living life with what nature gave him.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · The longevity of a story · October 7, 2024

excerpts.text: "I’m here for the things I’m never gonna see. Documenting art, writings, etc. on Bitcoin with the potential to stand the test of time and outlive all of us, is something I find super exciting. Being a part of that in its nascent state is even more special, and as someone who always loved history, background stories, and collecting things - I’m dreaming of a day where digital archeologists get as passionate about my work as I am myself today. That they start digging, connecting dots and forming the puzzle of my works. Dreams aside, inspiring people in any ways would be amazing for sure."
excerpts.caption: Interview excerpt · Legacy and future readers · Fabled, October 7, 2024

excerpts.text:
5:52pm:
I lost my chain a few weeks back while I was still in Sin City. 
God knows what happened, even I have no clue how I lost it. 

5:55pm:
I put this one on-chain 
So it never leaves me again.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · A lost chain · October 23, 2024

entries.title: Peak Audacity: letting the triangle speak
paragraphs: Peak Audacity uses the same algorithm as the informal Stress Test group, but abandons the usual rectangular format for a triangle. Its geometry expresses a feeling of audacity that bothered the artist that day.
The HTML note is deliberately minimal: “LMAO, no comment!” The shape is left to carry what a longer explanation might have settled too quickly.

entries.title: La Tête Dans Les Étoiles: from delusion to conviction
paragraphs: An April 2023 declaration—“I am delusional”—returns in an October 2024 poem about conviction and possibility. The gap between the two dates is part of the work, recording a thought as it changes over time.

entries.title: Ma ville en quatre temps: a soundtrack for the seasons
paragraphs: The four works carry musical references in their HTML writing. Un Été à Montréal brings together songs by Dubmatique, Taktika with Manu Boivin, and Treizième Étage with Rad.

L’Hiver, la nuit has M83’s Midnight City. Retour en classe has Mac DeMarco’s On the Level. L’Automne s’envole has Washed Out’s Feel It All Around. Music gives another route into the changing atmosphere of the city.

entries.title: Minute, papillon!: writing within the editions
paragraphs: The twenty-one editions are individually numbered and signed. Each has its own small note alongside the original poem.
They were inscribed as children of the original 1/1, which was then burned to OP_RETURN. The visual may be shared, but each inscription has its own place and writing within that structure.

entries.title: BEST BEFORE: a summer of revisions
paragraphs: The April 29 sketch began with an expiry date stamped at the bottom. Through June and August, the visual work moved away from that early proposal as the concept, code and textures developed together.
The dated comparison offers a view of that movement. The complete diary preserves the conversations and decisions behind it.

images.caption: April 29, June 19, June 20, June 30 and August 18, 2025.

entries.title: BEST BEFORE: choosing when a work begins
paragraphs: A sealed work leaves the decision of when to begin with its collector. Opening can happen quietly, or become a shared event. The lifespan then unfolds in Bitcoin block time.

The artist imagines an exhibition whose opening is the activation and whose closing follows the work’s expiry. These are possibilities for experiencing the work: a collector’s decision can become part of its story.

entries.title: Long Canyon and gOat
paragraphs: ORDINALLY mixed Long Canyon from one of his own inscribed landscape photographs. His involvement also produced a palette tool that helped the collaboration.
Lemonhaze later mixed gOat from another photograph ORDINALLY shared. The capital O is a nod to his collaborator. The resulting BB outputs preserve two different responses to that exchange.

images.caption: A BEST BEFORE output in Long Canyon.
A BEST BEFORE output in gOat.

entries.title: Opening BEST BEFORE Nº33
paragraphs: On October 5, 2025, Lemonhaze opened his first BEST BEFORE: Nº33, in palette SS, with a lifespan of seventy-one years at activation.
Its signature carries a line from the collaboration about trusting visual instinct. The artist became a participant in the same decision he had given to collectors.

images.caption: BEST BEFORE Nº33 · AI-generated framed presentation study, shown on the artist’s website.

entries.title: Montreal at Suburbs Gallery
paragraphs: In August 2025, Montreal was presented at Suburbs Gallery in the city that gave the series its memories. The short walkthrough shows the works arranged across screens around the room.
The exhibition was curated by Gamma. The collection had remained in the artist’s personal vault after its January 2024 inscription, before returning to its subject’s city for this presentation.

entries.title: Gentleman Nº11: front and reverse
paragraphs: The front and annotated reverse document a 40 × 40 cm print of Gentleman Nº11 on Hemp 290gsm paper.
These photographs record a specific physical object and its presentation, alongside the digital artwork.

images.caption: The annotated reverse of the print.

entries.title: Blood, Lemon & Tango in a collector’s home
paragraphs: A collector shared this video of a framed Blood, Lemon & Tango print with a SATSCHIP. Moving from the frame to a phone, the video shows the physical presentation alongside its digital record.

video.title: Blood, Lemon & Tango in a collector’s home

entries.title: Curating for a different setting
paragraphs: In July 2026, Lemonhaze spent a day curating eighty-nine paint-engine outputs for a physical project and making presentation mockups.
These studies explore how selected images might sit on a wall. They record a proposed presentation, rather than a completed installation.

entries.title: When “work in progress” became the idea
paragraphs: On March 31, 2023, Lemonhaze shared a realisation with artist Kenneth Burris: Gentlemen would always remain a work in progress because becoming a gentleman could never be a finished task.
The message captures the moment a personal aspiration became the continuing structure of the collection. The reflection was shared publicly again in November 2025.

images.caption: The Gentlemen collection, shown with the later reflection.

entries.title: Making images with a musician’s approach
paragraphs: Lemonhaze’s background moves through guitar, electronic music, drawing and painting. Dr Dre and Daft Punk are references for a way of assembling a work: selecting sounds, tools and layers to reach a particular feeling.

That approach continues in the visual work. Texture, samples, drawings and code can be combined according to what the image needs. Architecture, interiors, city views and memories also shape the direction.

images.caption: Layers and sampled forms in a later digital surface.

entries.title: The writing travels with the image
paragraphs: Writing runs through the body of work. Poems, passing thoughts, and journal entries live inside the artworks, most often in their HTML headers. Inscribed alongside the images, they form a digital, immutable journal.

The recurring “A Day in the Life” passages record the life around the making: daily routines, places, encounters, doubts, and progress in the studio. Verse sits beside these dated notes, holding a moment or a state of mind. Together, they carry a story that continues from one work to the next.
For Lemonhaze, the image and its words can work like music and lyrics: each carries something the other cannot.

entries.title: A digital work for a digital life
paragraphs: Much of Lemonhaze’s work is made on a laptop and intended to be experienced on a screen. Its pixel arrangement and textures belong to that setting.
Physical prints are another possible encounter with particular works, but the original digital viewer remains central—especially when an image responds to interaction, code or time.

entries.title: Un Indien dans la ville, before Ordinals
paragraphs: Un Indien dans la ville dates to 2011, before the Bitcoin inscriptions. An older room photograph and a close view preserve part of the artist’s physical work from that period.
The pictures connect the later digital practice with a longer history of making music, paintings and sketches.

images.caption: Un Indien dans la ville in an earlier room photograph.
A close view shared in December 2024.

entries.title: The space around the work
paragraphs: The spaces around the work are ordinary and personal: a laptop among chairs, plants, a guitar and a surfboard; later, a compact desk in Vietnam.
These photographs record places in which the practice continued, with the tools close at hand.
By July 2026, the workspace was a standing desk on a Montreal balcony, with the Farine Five Roses sign visible at night.

images.alt: Laptop on a standing desk on a Montreal balcony at night, with the Farine Five Roses sign in the distance
images.caption: Montreal workspace at night · July 2026.

entries.title: A provenance tree shaped by time
paragraphs: Lemonhaze’s provenance follows the chronology of the work: parents for collections and an annual parent for individual pieces. The organisation preserves the path of the practice, with its changes and irregularities.

An annual parent can be burned to close a year, while the inscribed works remain part of the artistic record. The history of what was made and the number of works circulating answer different questions.

images.caption: Gentleman Special Edition 2025, the annual parent.
The 2025 group, shared with the year-end reflection.

entries.title: Lost in Bangkok: a poem at 1:01 am
paragraphs: A walk becomes a poem, moving between getting lost, losing control, and wanting to return to My Love. The words are dated 1:01 am, February 4, 2025, in Bangkok, and live in the artwork’s HTML header.

The entry has three parts: a poem, a song reference, and “A Day in The Life.” At 1:43 am, the writing turns to the next day’s departure for Ayutthaya. Verse and the ordinary details of a journey share the same inscription.

excerpts.text:
Went out for a walk and got lost.
That’s when I met Chanchanok.

Did all.
Not done.
Now more.

Straying away from My Love.

A Dream, Thank God, the smoke,
Now I’m back to square one.

How far
are you
willing
to go?

Bring me back to My Love.

Only when I lose control.
Nothing worse for my soul.

Next move
is yours,
Where are
you now?

I’m lost in Bangkok
excerpts.caption: The complete poem · Lost in Bangkok · February 4, 2025

entries.title: Chanchanok’s Temple: a poem and a promise
paragraphs: Ten days after Lost in Bangkok, Chanchanok returns in another poem. Time slips by, the temple becomes a place of retreat, and the final lines make a promise to My Love.

The HTML entry moves from the poem to “Duality,” then to “A Day in The Life.” A 3:00 am Valentine’s Day note switches between French and English, recording sleeplessness, absence, and a work on display in Paris. These fragments remain with the image as a record of that night.

excerpts.text:
Losing track of why
And time is passing by

Different kind of vibes
My temple in the jungle.

Dreaming of Chanchanok
A different kind of high

I promise this is the last time
I’m soon back to you My Love.
excerpts.caption: The complete poem · Chanchanok’s Temple · February 14, 2025

entries.title: Le Confessionnal: moments of a day
paragraphs: Le Confessionnal moves between “Redemption Road” and “A Day in the Life”: personal reflection alongside the sounds of the city, lost sleep, and progress on the image. The writing shifts between French and English, with times marking its changes of thought.

At 6:39 pm, uncertainty takes the form of a short passage about exploration. Seven minutes later, the entry returns to the artwork and the hope of finishing it that night. The image holds both the reflection and the day that produced it.

excerpts.text:
This is uncharted territory.
There are uncertainties, and
we never know what’s waiting
for us on the other side.
Like explorers sailing the ocean,
riding waves to new continents.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · 6:39 pm · Le Confessionnal (Sin City) · September 17, 2024

entries.title: Cashback: beauty and disillusionment
paragraphs: Written in Vung Tau at the end of 2024, Cashback records a moment of disillusionment with the art market. Its reference to the film Cashback turns the idea of a painter capturing beauty toward the ugliness the artist felt around him.
The entry holds affection for making art alongside frustration with the world around it. Kept inside the work, the writing preserves that state of mind at a particular time.

excerpts.text:
I love what I’m doing, don’t get me wrong, but as the days goes by, I’m becoming more and more cynical about this.

If in the movie Cashback (2006) they say a painter captures beauty, I’m here today capturing what’s ugly.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · Cashback · December 19, 2024

entries.title: Duet Tacet: love through the seasons
paragraphs: At 3:03 am, somewhere between Saigon and Osaka, a poem returns to the beginning of a relationship on rue St-Charles. Winter gives way to spring, and the idea of love frozen in time gives way to love that keeps changing.
The passage moves between French and English. It belongs to the artist’s own writing in the first part of the inscription; a separately credited song follows later.

excerpts.text:
Ce soir je suis dans les airs, entre Saigon et Osaka,
et encore une fois j’me dit que les amours naissent les soirs d’hivers.
Mais pourtant c’est au printemps que t’es venu me rejoindre sur la rue St-Charles.
If I thought love is something that freeze in time,
maintenant je sais que ca grandi pour vrai après le gel, au printemps. 

T’avais mis une robe pour moi, et je t’aimais déjà.
Si j’osais pas le dire, et si je gardais mon air désinvolte,
c’était simplement parce que j’étais jeune et innocent.
J’avais peur de toi et de l’effet que tu avais sur moi.
Je ne voulais pas croire que l’amour est quelque chose qui évolue constamment,
un peu comme les quatre saisons au Canada. Je sais tu me l'as dit tant de fois.

Dès le début, t’as choisis l’amour.
Alors que moi j’ai pris les pires chemins,
parsemés de hauts et de bas, de lust et de charmes viscérale.
Mais tranquillement j’te rejoint mon coeur et je m’en vais nul part ailleurs.

Your smile, your kiss
and your voice whispering soft words.
I can still feel it in my bones.
Meaningless and meaningful all at once,
but not meaningless dans le mauvais sens.
I know what I’m saying doesn't sense.
But sometimes I miss the old days.
excerpts.caption: Complete opening poem · Duet Tacet · 2025-01-15

entries.title: Birthday Girl: a card inside the artwork
paragraphs: A birthday card with a handmade lotus opens the inscription. Its short dedication places the beauty of a person’s heart above the number of years passing.
The journal that follows becomes a shared page: Cathy adds her own words directly in the editor. The artwork keeps the card and the conversation together.

excerpts.text:
Un an de plus, mais ce n'est qu'un chiffre.
La beauté de ton coeur et la générosité de ton âme,
eux restent à jamais les mêmes. Bonne fête, My Love.
Je t'aime
Fred xxx
excerpts.caption: Complete dedication · Birthday Girl · 2025-05-25

entries.title: Night Owl: the stories in ordinary encounters
paragraphs: A late meal in Osaka becomes a long journal entry about solitude and the need for company. By the end, the night’s encounters lead to another ambition: writing films.
This passage turns toward the small details of human interaction and the stories they might hold. Music is already part of the imagined film.

excerpts.text: Off-topic, but thinking about this reminds me how I’d love to be writing movies at some point in my life. As I said before, there’s something beautiful about living life in the wild. The little details and nuances of the many interactions we have as humans are worth exploring beyond the surface - stories and moments that may appear banal at first glance are often the most interesting ones. Oh, and the movies I’ll write will undoubtedly have good soundtrack, it’s a must.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · Night Owl · 2025-01-20

entries.title: Wilderness: learning to see the light
paragraphs: At 8:08 pm, a short passage turns wilderness into a way of finding direction. Moonlight, silence, and instinct guide the movement from uncertainty toward recognition.
The writing is dated in Puerto Escondido and kept in the same inscription as the image.

excerpts.text:
In the wilderness, we are guided by the moon and the stars.
The path is never given, it is revealed in fragments of light.
Silence becomes the compass, instinct the map.
And by morning, we realize we were never truly lost.
Only learning to see the light again.
excerpts.caption: Complete 8:08 pm passage · Wilderness · 2026-04-08

entries.title: Self-Portrait: a gift to a future reader
paragraphs: Three lines imagine the self hidden inside a gift, waiting for someone in the future to open it. The next section answers with a single sentence: “Until then, it's just void.”
The journal continues across several dates in February, ending with the decision to inscribe more. The verse addresses a future reader while the notes record the days of making.

excerpts.text:
i hide inside the quantum gift
lately the days are silent and swift
a gift to someone in the future who can open it
excerpts.caption: Complete opening verse · Self-Portrait · 2026-02-27

entries.title: Insaisissable Mirage: the next horizon
paragraphs: The opening asks what keeps a person going when every reached goal gives way to another. A few short lines turn ambition into a repeating movement.
The rest of the entry brings that question back to daily life: working on the balcony, cooking, and speaking with My Love. Near the end, another small passage describes a sunset as a mirage.

excerpts.text:
What do you tell yourself to carry on?

The goals I set for myself
Once I reached them
I chase the next
It never stops
It’s my fuel
It’s a vibe
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · Insaisissable Mirage · 2024-11-03

entries.title: Kowloon: a sunset in real time
paragraphs: A memory of Hong Kong opens the entry, but the journal soon returns to the balcony in front of the artist. At 5:03 pm, the work is ready to inscribe and an orange-peach sun is slipping behind the clouds.
By 5:09 pm, the sun has disappeared. These few minutes give the writing the immediacy of a journal still being written.

excerpts.text:
5:03pm:
C'est presque le crépuscule, Cathy vient tout just de rentrer d'une seance de yoga et moi de j'ai terminé cette piece que je m'apprete à mettre on-chain.
On est sur le balcon, on regarde le soleil orange peach... mais là il commence à etre complement couvert par les nuages.

5:09pm:
Boom, le soleil est diparus dans les nuages.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · Kowloon · 2024-11-11

entries.title: Soir d’hiver: remembering the air of Montreal
paragraphs: Fresh air, moonlight, and rosy cheeks bring Montreal back through the senses. The note moves from the idea of love beginning on winter evenings to the feeling of missing a birthplace.
The memory remains vivid even after nearly three years away. A brief switch into English marks the passing time.

excerpts.text: J’ai toujours pensé que les amours naissent les soirs d'hiver.  L’air frais, la lune qui éclaire, les joues rosées, “J’erre” et “Je ne sais pas” de Dumas. Quelque part à Montréal... probablement dans le vieux port. Je peux encore sentir l’air de la ville, près du fleuve, et entendre la nuit même si ça fait bientôt 3 ans que je n’y suis pas retourné. Time is passing by. Elle me manque ma terre natale.
excerpts.caption: Complete artist note · Soir d'hiver

entries.title: Saint-Laurent: one photograph, two lives
paragraphs: Cathy’s photograph began on a bicycle ride from Brossard toward Montreal, along the Saint-Laurent. It became the cover for a song before returning as material for a visual work.
The note also records an intention: to bring photographs from upcoming travels into the artist’s p5.js structures. A shared memory opens a new direction in the work.

excerpts.text: The original photo was taken by my love, Cathy. We were biking to Montreal from Brossard along the Fleuve Saint-Laurent a morning somewhere in 2014 or 2015, I can't remember exactly. And this photo ended up being the cover photo for one of my song titled 'Saint-Laurent' that I published on Soundcloud at the time. If you're looking you might still be able to find that song.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · Saint-Laurent

entries.title: Watson Esplanade: the way home
paragraphs: Without a car in Surfers Paradise, walking and cycling shaped the days. Watson Esplanade was part of the route home, and the writing remembers it through the people and moments along the way.
The place holds the movement of an earlier life on the Gold Coast: friends, conversation, laughter, and plans.

excerpts.text: Back when we lived in Surfers Paradise we didn't have a car. We were on WHV, it was bicycle or often just walking. We lived both on Sunset and Sunrise boulevard and the Watson Eslanade was on our path home/toAnywhere. Needless to say there was quite a few memorable moments on that esplanade. Walking with friends, drinking, dreaming, smoking, laughing. My time on the Gold Coast was surely some of the best of time of my life so far.
excerpts.caption: Complete artist note · Watson Esplanade

entries.title: Orange Why Not: missing a time without returning
paragraphs: This note holds two feelings together: missing an earlier life and not wanting to go back to it. Gratitude for the people and experiences remains, even as the artist recognises a change in how he lives.
The language slips between English and French as nostalgia becomes something more difficult to name.

excerpts.text: I'm feeling nostalgique right now. I miss some period of my life but I don't want to go back there either, weird feeling. The connections made with other humans, the vibrant lifestyle I had, I'm grateful for all of it. Life really is a buffet, how much of it do you want it? My lifestyle is healtier now but I can't help it but feel nostalgique, and perhaps sometimes even melancholic.
excerpts.caption: Complete artist note · Orange Why Not

entries.title: Avant le Crépuscule: the other side of a sunset
paragraphs: On the eve of a tenth anniversary, a sunset suggests a life still waiting on the other side. The writing holds that uncertainty beside the continuity of a long relationship.
A dedication to Cathy interrupts the questions. The passage ends by asking whether everything might still be possible.

excerpts.text: I feel like there's this whole other life waiting for me on the other side of that sunset, but I can't tell what it is, and if it's something I want. All I know is that tomorrow is gonna be the 10th Anniversary of my relationship with Cathy. Je t'aime, mon coeur. It's crazy how time is passing by. We're young when we met, and yet despite being salt and pepper I still see us as being young. What if we can have it all?
excerpts.caption: Complete artist note · Avant le Crepuscule

entries.title: Rabbi: a note of thanks
paragraphs: A short acknowledgment records help received while experimenting with generative art. Rabbi offered technical guidance when the artist was struggling.
The inscription preserves that exchange and the value of strangers sharing what they know.

excerpts.text: Something I always appreciate with the Bitcoin (and broader crypto) community is how knowledge is shared and how strangers are not shy to help. Rabbi came to me and offered his help knowing I was struggling with a few (or many lol) technical stuff regarding the generative art I've been experimenting with lately. Thanks Rabbi
excerpts.caption: Complete artist note · Rabbi

entries.title: Smooth Sailor: before the rain
paragraphs: At 10:30 pm, the plan is simple: inscribe the work, then watch a film with My Love. The day has included window-shopping and a walk across the Dragon Bridge.
As rain begins, the note pauses on the wish to stay in Da Nang. The entry holds the work alongside an ordinary evening.

excerpts.text:
I need to put this one on-chain and jump in bed to watch a movie with My Love.
Earlier today we did some window-shopping and walked the dragon bridge.
I love Da Nang and Vietnam in general, I kinda wish we could stay.
It's starting to rain. May it rain the good thing in a few weeks?
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · Smooth Sailor · 2025-09-05

entries.title: O-Swirl: a first night at Casa Flamingo
paragraphs: The first night at Casa Flamingo brings back childhood weekends in the forest with his father. The house is still unfinished, and its makeshift comforts call up another way of living.
Later entries address a friend and collaborator, but this passage stays with the first night: a memory of Rawdon, then tea and moonlight on the balcony.

excerpts.text:
This brought back old memories of when I was young - the weekends deep in the forest with my father in Rawdon, Québec. 

Les coureurs de bois…

Sleeping in a wood shack with no proper toilet - setting up snare trap during the day and watching movies at night. But watch out for the deerflies!

Now I’m drinking tea and smoking on the balcony while watching the moon shine - grateful.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · Paint Engine v0.2 [O-Swirl] · 2025-11-07

entries.title: Faux-Chat: ideas becoming tangible
paragraphs: This entry records the excitement of finding tools that make more ideas possible. The artist reflects on having once wished to live in another era, then feeling unexpectedly at home in this one.
The writing becomes impatient with itself: there is more to build. It captures a moment when learning, imagining, and making feel closely connected.

excerpts.text:
I think I was born at the right moment in time for who I am.
You know, I often said I wished I was born in a past era etc...
and yet now I realize I'm right where I fit the most.
These new tools, what they enable - how things such as ideas, visions and concept
that usually either required insane level of coding skills and/or literal human and financial resources
now can be done by sharing my mind with a computer.
What we call, artificial intelligence - large language model and agents.

I swear, it's hard to find the word to descript the capacity unlocked.
I'm making an effort to write my mind so much I just want to keep building more.
The possibility of converting my minds into something tangible.
Building. Creating. Full of potential.
I love this shit right now.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · Paint Engine v1.03 [Faux-Chat] · 2026-01-23

entries.title: Gaijin: two lines about belonging
paragraphs: Two lines bring together the foreigner and the coureur de bois. The note leaves the question of home open, locating the speaker in movement.
Its brevity gives the words the weight of a small self-portrait.

excerpts.text:
Wherever I go, I’m a foreigner
I have no home, I’m a coureur de bois
excerpts.caption: Complete artist note · Gaijin

entries.title: Tea Pot: a memory at first sip
paragraphs: A cup of bubble tea brings back Taipei in 2024. Four short lines turn taste into a memory of a place and a moment.
Written in Montreal two years later, the entry also includes a birthday greeting to his father. Travel memory and family life share the page.

excerpts.text:
It was love at first sip.
Bubble tea in Taipei.
With something to smoke.
Somewhere in 2024.
excerpts.caption: Complete opening verse · Tea Pot · 2026-09-13

entries.title: Dai-Rei: walking into a series
paragraphs: Long walks through Osaka become the starting point for Tōri no Roji. The writing notices the contrast between busy streets and smaller, quieter passages.

Near the end of the entry, those observations become decisions about the image: neon, restrained pathways, new palettes, and variations in the algorithm. The journal records how looking turns into making.

excerpts.text:
All that to say, I ended up being inspired very quickly by what surrounds me. Touches of neon and all the charming alleys and whatnot,
that led me to spend time tweaking my algorithm to make something that captures all of this charm I’m seeing around.
A mix of colorful lights and more sober pathways, all of which I'm constantly exploring when I go out to walk in town.

These works are what came out of this so far.
I'll be inscribing more palettes and variations in the coming days/weeks,
as I find more things to say and share about my stay in Osaka.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · Dai-Rei · 2025-01-21

entries.title: Fisherman: someday, a fishing trip
paragraphs: The opening question is about waiting. The journal answers with a new father still taking in the change, imagining a fishing trip with his child one day.
Two unpolished lines keep the feeling close to the moment it was written, at 11:29 pm.

excerpts.text:
I don't think I realize I'm father yet.
But I hope we'll go fishing someday.
excerpts.caption: Complete 11:29 pm passage · Fisherman · 2026-09-11

entries.title: From Berlin to Saigon: following the ink
paragraphs: The title traces a developing visual language. The Berlin series, drawn in 2023 from memories of a short stay in 2018, changed the way Lemonhaze thought about composition. Dark, ink-like forms and textured surfaces became an idea to pursue across different tools.

In Hong Kong in June 2024, a visit to HOKMA brought paper, ink, and brush pens into the story. Unable to read the characters in the artworks he saw, he experienced their shapes as abstraction. That encounter gave the forms he was seeking another point of reference.

The HTML writing connects these experiences to hand drawing, AI, and experiments with p5.js. It also names earlier works across several collections, leaving a trail through the practice. An output made in Saigon becomes a moment to look back at how the idea arrived there.

excerpts.text:
Berlin was really about making mementos of my short stay in Berlin back in 2018.
Each pieces were digitally hand drawn, and have their own story, but that's for another day.
I'm talking about it here because it had a direct influence on the way I think about composition ever since.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · Memories becoming compositions

excerpts.text:
For quite some time I’ve been interested in these dark/black ink,
Abstract reflective scenery/structure, half fake-Rorschach things, half-nothing.
I like how they bring contrast to what I see on my canvas, it's my mirage.
Superposed on minimal layout with vintage textures, I like even more.

So, while it started by digitally hand drawing like in Berlin (or even physically)
I quickly explored other ways to get things done.
With AI, I did a lot of work that reinforced this idea I had/have in mind.
But "code only" aka p5js, quickly became my goal - part for the challege it showed to be,
Part to espouse the constraints of Bitcoin by increasing efficiency with code-only.

Things connected even more in Hong-Kong, June 2024, when I visited HOKMA and purchased a few items like papers, ink and brush pen.
Because I couldn't read what was writen on most artworks, the black ink characters on silk were abstract to my eyes.
Yet the art, the feel, was speaking to me in so many ways. Part of the vibes I've been chasing ever since.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · From drawing to code, through Hong Kong

excerpts.text:
With this piece here today (October 29, 2024 - 6:19pm) I'm taking a moment to show a glimpse into the evolution and progress of this idea,
by showing you this output that I generated a couple of days ago when I was in Saigon making experimentation within my current working project.

From Berlin to Saigon, made with code

Cheers to Art on Bitcoin
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · October 29, 2024

entries.title: Under Construction: a life taking shape
paragraphs: The journal begins with reflections on BEST BEFORE and the passing of things: attention, careers, relationships, and time. Working on the Paint Engine offers pleasure, while writing becomes a way of speaking to someone in the future.

Across several days, the entries move between short poems, questions about permanence, and the ordinary act of showing up to work. Then, on January 8, Cathy tells him she is pregnant. The writing changes direction toward joy, hope, and the wish to tell his mother.
Read through the journal, “Under Construction” takes on another meaning. An engine is being developed while a new family life begins to take shape.

excerpts.text:
There's something unique and hard to describe
About the act of inscribing my works and my words.

One reason I do it so religiously is perhaps to speak to someone in the future: 
sometimes myself, sometimes others far down the road, long after I'm gone.

This raises the question:
what are the odds of Bitcoin surviving 50 years, 100 years, or 1,000 years? 
The format of the work, the language of the code, the language of the words spoke?

So many questions...
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · Writing to a future reader · January 5, 2026

excerpts.text:
2:22pm:
I’m speechless, in the best way possible.
Twenty-twenty-six is off to a good start
My Love just told me she’s pregnant.|
May this be the best thus far.
Thank you My Love.
Thank you God.

3:01pm:
There are moments that quietly redraw the entire map of your life.

7:27pm:
Suddenly, all I feel is joy and hope.
And I can't wait to tell my mom.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · January 8, 2026

entries.title: Flashback: the beginning, found again
paragraphs: Looking through an old email account brings back songs, screenshots, photographs, and music demos. Flashback gathers these traces into one inscription, placing early writing beside a reflection written years later in Kuala Lumpur.

The opening returns to “CATHY ATM,” dated October 29, 2013. Its hopes for travel, a shared life, and children sit beside the uncertainty of asking whether she will come along. The inscription also preserves other credited voices and returns to the dedication behind Lotus.

Near the end, a small discovery connects the periods: the earlier work was signed FNSL, before the FNST signature. The journal closes by naming the act of inscribing these memories as a way of keeping the beginning of their story.

excerpts.text:
I wanna take you away
Go far and start a new life
Make new friends and never come back
That’s how I feel with you baby

I feel that this could have no end
Having kids, diner and breakfast
A middle class work with PRESIDENT LOVE

You may think I speak too fast, but I’m not.
It took me so long to write this down
As long as it took me to give you the crown.

I’m not counting the time anymore with you
My feelings are strong enough to know what I want

ONE LOVE and a STRONG ONE

… Now that it’s all said, I’m scared.
Can I ever drive you there… will you join me…
Are we gonna rock this out?
Are we gonna rock this out?

Cathy at the moment
excerpts.caption: Original song text · CATHY ATM · October 29, 2013

excerpts.text:
8:42pm:
Going through these old emails, screenshots, photos and short recordings of music demo on my old email account “Kamlung” (from the Chinese restaurant in Longueuil) reminded me that I used to sign my stuff FNSL instead of FNST as I do nowadays.

9:37pm:
I’m gonna finish this and inscribe it for eternity - this was the start of our story.

Je t’aime, Cathy.
My Little Dragon.
My Love. Ma Lotus.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · Finding the old recordings · May 13, 2025

entries.title: Griffintown: back in the city
paragraphs: After nearly five years away, Lemonhaze returns to Montreal. The first entry looks out over the Lachine Canal: people walking, cycling, playing volleyball, and moving through the neighbourhood. Five Roses becomes part of the view from the balcony.

The next evening brings a short poem about salmon served on a cardboard box in the new living room. Later, the journal watches the city at night: a piano, a reader, someone working at a desk, lights turning on and off. Small domestic scenes give the return its texture.

Against that continuing life, he notices how much his own days have changed. With a son on the way and less time to make art, the writing records both the pleasure of being home and the wish to keep creating.

excerpts.text:
Un saumon romantique.
Sur une boite de carton.
Dans notre nouveau salon.
Un peu cliché mais pratique.

La belle étoile dans le vide
Un ptit piknik, un bixi
Le temps de dire merci
My Love on est d'retour en ville
excerpts.caption: Complete poem · June 3, 2026

excerpts.text:
At night on my balcony, the view is as good as it is during the day, in fact possibly better.
The red flashing Five Roses sign is great but what I like most is the cinematic view of the building on the other side of the street, facing East.
I can see inside all the apartments, the people living their lives at their own rythmn. The lights from the inside contrasting on the dark sky.
The first apartment on the left, around the 14th floor, has an elegant black grand piano in the living room.
A couple of levels lower on the right, I can see a man absorbed by a book from his cozy reading corner by the large window.
And just abov, someone working on a laptop at their desk in the bedroom. Some lights turning on and others turning off.
Always the ticking clock. It's dark but down on the ground people are still playing beach volleyball.
excerpts.caption: Excerpt · The city at night · June 15, 2026
